findings.title: Migration crashes when embed_category is unset
findings.body: The migration does execute(...)[0]['id'] on the embed_category lookup (and the same pattern for uncategorized_category_id). Site settings at their default are often not stored as rows, and a renamed or missing category also yields no row, so [0] is nil and the migration raises NoMethodError before the category_id == 0 fallback. Upgrading a typical site that never set embed_category fails and never creates embeddable_hosts.

findings.title: Migrated hosts are not normalized and are interpolated into SQL
findings.body: Existing embeddable_hosts values are inserted raw with string interpolation. The old allow-list stripped http(s):// and paths at compare time, and the new model only normalizes on validation, so values like http://example.com or https://example.com/path are stored verbatim. EmbeddableHost.record_for_host compares lower(host) to URI#host, so those rows never match and embedding/import silently stops after upgrade. A host containing a quote also breaks the INSERT or injects SQL. Normalize (scheme, path, case) and use bound parameters.

findings.title: Import passes category id through the category-name option
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import now sets PostCreator's category: to eh.try(:category_id). The previous embed_category setting was a category name, and PostCreator's :category option looks up by name; the id belongs in category_id:. Imported embed topics will not land in the host's category (they fall through to uncategorized or fail the name lookup), which defeats the feature this PR adds.

findings.title: Host allow-list comparison is case-sensitive on the referer
findings.body: record_for_host queries lower(host) = ? but passes uri.host unchanged, and before_validation does not downcase the stored host. A stored host Example.com compared to a referer host example.com (or the reverse) does not match, so EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? rejects a host the admin saved. The same lookup is used for comment embedding and TopicRetriever, so those hosts cannot embed or import. Downcase both sides. Ports allowed by the format regex are also stored (example.com:8080) while URI#host omits the port, so those rows never match either.

findings.title: before_validation crashes when host is nil
findings.body: before_validation calls self.host.sub! without a presence check. Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host assigns params[:embeddable_host][:host] directly, so a create/update with a missing or null host raises NoMethodError instead of a validation error.

findings.title: Update and destroy 500 when the host id is missing
findings.body: update and destroy load EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and then call save_host(host) or host.destroy with no nil check. An unknown id raises NoMethodError (500) instead of a 404. save_host also does not check that the category_id refers to a real category, so a bogus id is persisted and later imports attach topics to a missing category.

findings.title: Hydrating *_ids throws when the value is null
findings.body: The new plural branch always calls obj[k].map and then deletes the *_ids key. Any rest payload with a null or non-array *_ids field (not just the fruit fixtures) throws during find/findAll and drops the raw ids even when lookup fails, so embedded has-many hydration can break unrelated models.
